messages:
maria: Hey -- seeing gRPC streaming sessions silently stall between pods on different nodes in eu-west1. Happens ~10-30s into long-lived streams, client sees `EOF` / `connection reset by peer`. No app exception. Logs show repeated `transport: read tcp ...: connection reset by peer` and a bunch of retransmits in tcp stats. :eyes:
ops-bot: Alert: network-errors high on nodes gpu-eu-02 and gpu-eu-07, rx-dropped spiking, PMTU probe failures detected by kernel on several interfaces.
ben: Any recent CNI or host MTU changes? We rolled cilium 1.14 last week with vxlan overlay on these nodes. Could be path MTU mismatch + encapsulation overhead. If ICMP 'frag needed' is getting dropped (by host firewall or cloud infra), PMTU discovery can fail -> packets hit DF and get dropped, gRPC stalls while retransmits try smaller windows.
arjun: I ran a quick tcpdump on node gpu-eu-02 while reproing a stream. Saw ICMP type 3 code 4 messages being generated on the receiver end:
```
15:12:03.123456 IP 10.10.5.8 > 10.11.2.4: ICMP 3/4, mtu 1450
15:12:03.123458 IP 10.11.2.4 > 10.10.5.8: tcp 0  :-
```
But our iptables mangle table on gpu-eu-02 had a rule that was accidentally DROPing some ICMP (legacy cleanup rule). So PMTU replies never reached the sender.
katie: Nice catch. Can you paste `ip link` and `ip -s link` outputs + `ip route get`? Also check `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` -- we've seen it help in blackhole cases.
ben: For quick mitigation we can either: 1) tune CNI MTU down to account for vxlan overhead (e.g., set cilium MTU to 1450), or 2) allow the ICMP frag-needed through firewall, or 3) enable conservative `tcp_mtu_probing=1` on senders. Disabling GSO/GRO on problematic interfaces can also force smaller packets immediately (temporary).
maria: I checked host MTU: host nic is configured for jumbo (9000). Cilium's default vxlan overlay reduces payload MTU by 50 or so; if pod interface still assumes 9000 we get mismatches. Running `ip -s link show cilium_vxlan` shows fragmentation stats.
arjun: Also a wrinkle: a subset of nodes have Mellanox cards with RDMA enabled. With offloads enabled, large skbs can leave userland far bigger than path allows and kernel doesn't always generate ICMP early enough. On those nodes disabling GSO/GRO helped repro and recovery. Example commands we ran:
```
# show iface offload settings
etstat -i || true
ethtool -k eth0
# turn off GRO/GSO temporarily
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
# allow ICMP frag-needed
sudo iptables -I INPUT 1 -p icmp --icmp-type fragmentation-needed -j ACCEPT
# enable tcp probing
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
```
katie: Maria, can you push a canary change: allow ICMP frag-needed on host firewall + set `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on a couple nodes and lower Cilium MTU for canary pods to 1450? We'll watch streams.
maria: Canary applied on gpu-eu-02 and gpu-eu-07: allowed ICMP type3/code4, set probing=1. Also temporarily set cilium mtu to 1450 for the test pool. After that, streaming sessions recovered on the canary app (no stalls for ~20m) and retransmit rates dropped ~95% in Grafana. :tada:
ops-bot: Metrics update: retransmit_rate (canary) down from 18% -> 0.9% in last 15m, stream-success for canary up to 99.8%.
ben: Good. Long-term we should: 1) audit iptables rules in daemonset that manage host firewall (we had a cleanup rule that was too broad), 2) set sensible CNI MTU defaults for vxlan/encap that account for jumbo/encap overhead, 3) add an MTU verification job in node-recon to detect mismatch between host nic MTU and CNI MTU, 4) document RDMA offload interactions and recommend disabling GSO/GRO for problematic flows or tune NIC offload heuristics.
arjun: I'll open a follow-up to disable the aggressive DROP rule and add explicit accept for ICMP frag-needed + add e2e test to simulate PMTU blackhole.
katie: Also add runbook steps (disable offloads, set tcp_mtu_probing, fallback CNI mtu) and assign oncall rotation to validate fixes during busy hours. Ticket: INFRA-1327.
maria: Thanks all. Leaving canary running for 6h, will rollback if we see regressions. If anyone sees related errors from other regions ping here. :eyes:
